 Gamecocks Back on the Road Saturday
 Share 
 Twitter 
 Facebook 
 Mail 
 Print 
 #1/1 South Carolina Gamecocks (5-0) 
 at
 Providence Friars (2-3) 
 Nov 21, 2026 
 |
 1:30 pm 
 Providence, RI | Alumni Hall 
 TV: 
 Peacock 
 RADIO: 
 B106.7 FM 
 ONLINE: 
 Tickets 
 Live Stats 
 Game Notes 
 Media Availability 
 COLUMBIA, SC – No. 1/1 South Carolina travels to New England for two games, beginning with a 1:30 p.m. tipoff at Providence on Sat., Nov. 21. The game will stream on Peacock.
   Gamecock Notables 
 Playing one of the toughest schedules in the nation with three games against ranked opponents in its first four outings, South Carolina’s offense is among the top-20 in the nation. The Gamecocks’ 91.0 points per game, which includes 91.3 per game against ranked teams, comes in 17th while their 49.3 percent field goal shooting is 18th. 
 The Gamecock frontcourt has been strong on the glass this season, ranking 25th in the nation in rebounding margin (+12.8). Four players have at least one double-digit rebounding game, led by Chloe Kitts who has three in her four outings so far this season.
 South Carolina is seventh in the nation in offensive rebounding percentage, reeling in 47.3 percent of its missed shots. Joyce Edwards paces the team with 3.8 offensive boards per outing, sixth-best in the SEC, and Chloe Kitts is one spot behind her in seventh place at 3.75. The Gamecocks have turned those offensive boards into 18.0 second-chance points per game.
 Senior guard Tessa Johnson earned SEC and USBWA Player of the Week honors for her efforts in last week’s wins at Clemson and over then-#3/3 Southern Cal. Her career-high 28 points against the Trojans included three 3s, which helped move her into fifth in the SEC at 2.6 made 3s per game. She is second in the league in 3-point percentage, hitting 52.0 percent from the arc this season.
 Junior All-American Joyce Edwards is coming off back-to-back 20-point games over three days this week, during which she shot 67.9 percent (19-of-28) from the field. She is 13th in the SEC in scoring average (17.2 ppg) and 10th in field goal percentage (.551) on the season.
 Sophomore guard Agot Makeer is growing into her starting role, balancing being a scorer and a playmaker. Over the last two games, she averaged 13.0 points and 5.5 assists while shooting 61.1 percent (11-of-18) from the field.
 Fifth-year forward Chloe Kitts’ three double-doubles – all in her last three games – rank eighth in the country.
 Sophomore forward Alicia Tournebize posted her first career double-double on Tuesday against FGCU, turning in career highs of 14 points and 13 rebounds in just 13 minutes on the court.
 By the Numbers
 5 – All five South Carolina starters were named to the Wooden Award Preseason Watchlist – 2 more players than any other team.
 8 –   Eight different Gamecocks have been the team’s top scorer in at least one quarter this season.
 38 – South Carolina’s 38 points in the second quarter against FGCU on Tuesday set the program record for single-quarter scoring.
 The Providence Series
 The Gamecocks won the series opener against Providence in a 96-55 decision in Columbia on December 28, 2025. Six Gamecocks finished in double-figure points, including guard Agot Makeer who posted a double-double.
 Road Ready
 South Carolina is 330-264 (.556) all-time in road games (some records prior to 1976-77 did not include location of games), including a 156-49 mark (.761) under head coach Dawn Staley, giving her the best road winning percentage in program history.
 Second Effort
 South Carolina is 23rd in the nation in offensive rebounding percentage, grabbing 17.4 offensive boards per game. It has turned those rebounds into 18.0 second-chance points per game, which ranks 12th in the nation. Those numbers go up against ranked opponents to 19.5 offensive boards yielding 21.0 points per game.
 The Gamecocks’ starting frontcourt of Joyce Edwards and Chloe Kitts lead the way on the offensive glass, ranking sixth and seventh, respectively, in the SEC in the category. Their combined 6.8 offensive rebounds per game have yielded points (field goal or free throw) 64.7 percent of the time.
 Committee Work
 While there has been a lot of outside talk about South Carolina’s lack of a traditional point guard, one of the best point guards of all-time in Dawn Staley has not been concerned. The “point guard by committee” philosophy has yielded an efficient offense that includes the team’s top scorers also serving as its top distributors, including a pair of post players. 
 Sophomore Agot Makeer leads the way with a 3.6 assist average coming alongside her career-best 12.6 points per game. Forward Chloe Kitts is next in line at 3.0 assists per game added to her 13.0 points per outing. Top scorer Joyce Edwards (17.2 ppg) averages 2.8 assists, and Tessa Johnson has her hands on nearly a quarter of the Gamecocks’ offense between her 16.6 points and 2.4 assists per game. Freshman Jerzy Robinson rounds out the crew at 2.2 assists to go with 10.0 points per game.
